adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding a non-default interface method makes every precompiled third-party grant factory throw AbstractMethodError during encoder post-initialization and can prevent server startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface has a new method `getShortcut()` added without a default implementation. In Java, adding a non-default method to an interface is a breaking change - any existing third-party implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that were compiled against the old interface will throw AbstractMethodError when this method is called. The DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() method iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls getShortcut() on each one, which would cause failures for any third-party grant implementations that haven't been recompiled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:87 — Removing the public Context(Context) constructor breaks existing grant extensions that clone the request context with a compile-time error or runtime NoSuchMethodError.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context class (lines 102-116 in the old code are deleted). This is a public API in server-spi-private, and any existing OAuth2GrantType extensions that use this copy constructor to clone the context would fail with NoSuchMethodError at runtime or compilation errors. The finding correctly identifies this as a breaking change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — The decoder hard-codes a six-character context although the grant factory contract neither enforces nor documents two-character shortcuts, so a custom grant can mint IDs that this same provider cannot decode.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a contract inconsistency. Looking at the diff: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is added with Javadoc saying 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but doesn't enforce length. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() at line 74 hard-codes 'encodedContext.length() != 6' check, which assumes exactly 2 chars each for sessionType, tokenType, and grantType shortcuts. If a custom grant implementation returns a shortcut that isn't exactly 2 characters, tokens created with that grant would fail to decode. The SessionType and TokenType enums do use 2-char shortcuts, but the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface has no such constraint documented or enforced.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding mandatory getShortcut() breaks every existing third-party grant factory at source level and triggers AbstractMethodError during encoder post-initialization for already-compiled providers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1054 — Unconditionally changing every access-token jti from a UUID to a prefixed colon-delimited value breaks consumers and event pipelines that validate or store the previously emitted UUID shape, with no compatibility or versioning switch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that TokenManager.java line 1054 changes from `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` to `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, which produces a prefixed format like 'onrtac:UUID' instead of a plain UUID. This is a real architectural concern - the change modifies the token ID format from a simple UUID to a structured format with session type, token type, and grant type prefixes. The finding correctly identifies this could break existing consumers expecting UUID format. However, this appears to be an intentional design change (new SPI for token context encoding), not a bug. It's a valid scope/compatibility concern about the change, making it an important non-bug issue rather than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — The decoder hard-codes a six-character header even though the grant-factory contract documents three-character shortcuts, so a conforming custom shortcut produces token IDs that the same provider cannot decode.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at the diff, the 6-character header is composed of: 2 chars for sessionType shortcut + 2 chars for tokenType shortcut + 2 chars for grantType shortcut = 6 total. The Javadoc for getShortcut() says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but all actual implementations in the diff use 2-character shortcuts (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt', 'ci', 'dg', 'pg', 'te', 'ro', 'pc'). The SessionType and TokenType enums also use 2-character shortcuts ('on', 'of', 'tr', 'un', 'rt', 'lt'). So the 6-character expectation (2+2+2) is consistent with the actual implementation. The Javadoc saying '3-letters' appears to be a documentation typo, not a contract violation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:87 — Removing the public Context(Context) constructor is an unversioned source- and binary-incompatible change for grant extensions that copy the invocation context.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor (lines 102-116 in the old code). This is a public API in server-spi-private, and removing it would break any external OAuth2GrantType extensions that relied on this constructor to copy context objects. While this is a valid API compatibility concern for extensions, it's not a 'bug' in the sense of incorrect behavior - the code will work correctly for internal usage. It's an important architectural/compatibility concern that should be addressed, making it an important_non_bug finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId, allowing a null raw ID to become the literal "null" in an encoded token identifier.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at AccessTokenContext.java lines 69-73, the constructor has: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"); - The second check validates grantType again with the wrong error message instead of validating rawTokenId. This means rawTokenId is never null-checked, and if null is passed, it would be stored and later converted to the string "null" when used in encodeTokenId() which concatenates it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The matcher reads indices 3-4 instead of 4-5 and returns false on equality, so it accepts token IDs carrying the wrong grant shortcut and fails to test the new encoding.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for AssertEvents.java lines 476-487, the matcher implementation has two bugs: 1) `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts characters at indices 3-4 (2 chars), but based on the token format shown in tests like 'trltcc:1234' where the grant shortcut is at positions 4-5 (0-indexed), this should be `substring(4, 6)`. 2) The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut MATCHES, which is inverted logic - it should return false when they DON'T match. These bugs mean the matcher will incorrectly accept tokens with wrong grant shortcuts and reject tokens with correct ones.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding an encoder-specific mandatory method to the existing grant-provider SPI makes initialization fail on previously compiled custom factories and couples every grant extension to one encoding scheme.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line 33). This is a breaking change for any existing custom implementations of this interface - they would fail to compile or load at runtime because they don't implement the new required method. This is a legitimate API compatibility concern for an SPI that external code may implement. The finding correctly identifies this as coupling grant extensions to the encoding scheme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — The decoder hard-codes a six-character header even though getShortcut is unconstrained and documented as usually three letters, so a compliant extension can emit token IDs this framework cannot decode.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real inconsistency: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() at line 74 hard-codes 'encodedContext.length() != 6' validation, expecting exactly 6 characters (2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType). However, OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' without enforcing a 2-character constraint. The existing implementations all use 2-character shortcuts (ac, cc, pg, pc, rt, ro, te, ci, dg), but the interface documentation is misleading and doesn't enforce this constraint. A custom extension following the 'usually 3-letters' documentation would produce tokens that cannot be decoded. This is a real defect in the contract between the interface documentation and the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:57 — Grant metadata crosses layers through a generic ClientSessionContext attribute populated manually at several issuance sites, so new or custom paths silently encode na unless they duplicate this hidden plumbing.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a design concern in the diff. The grant type is passed through ClientSessionContext.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...) at multiple manual call sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, TokenManager.validateToken, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient). If a new or custom grant type implementation doesn't include this setAttribute call, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext at line 57 will get null and default to UNKNOWN ('na'). This is a legitimate architectural concern about the fragility of the design - it requires manual coordination across multiple code paths. However, it's not a bug per se since the code handles the null case gracefully with a fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — Lazy grant registration mutates both lookup maps without the collision validation used at startup, allowing a deployed grant to overwrite a shortcut and change how already-issued IDs decode.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() methods (lines 103-138), when a new grant type is dynamically discovered, it's added to both maps without the collision validation that exists in postInit(). In postInit() (lines 68-79), there's explicit validation checking if grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size() to detect duplicate shortcuts. However, the lazy registration in lines 107-111 and 127-131 simply puts values into both maps without checking if a shortcut already exists, potentially allowing a newly deployed grant to overwrite an existing shortcut mapping. This could cause already-issued tokens to decode incorrectly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:54 — The encoder depends on a protocol-mapper base class for lightweight-token policy, forcing that mapper helper public and creating a reverse layer dependency that makes either subsystem harder to evolve independently.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java at line 54 calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), and the diff shows this method was changed from private/package-private to 'public static' in AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java (line 84). This creates a dependency from the encode package to the mappers package, which is a legitimate architectural concern. The encoder (a new SPI provider) now depends on a protocol mapper base class, which could make these subsystems harder to evolve independently. This is a valid design/architecture concern grounded in the actual code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Invoking the newly abstract getShortcut method on every discovered grant factory makes upgrades fail at startup with AbstractMethodError when an existing third-party grant provider was compiled against the prior SPI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` (line +31-35 in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java). In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), line 74 calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on all OAuth2GrantType provider factories. Any third-party grant provider compiled against the previous SPI version (without getShortcut()) would cause AbstractMethodError at runtime when this code executes during startup. This is a real binary compatibility issue - adding abstract methods to interfaces breaks existing implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:75 — Startup accepts shortcuts of any length even though decoding requires a six-character context prefix, so a custom grant can issue token IDs that this framework cannot later decode.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is valid. In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), shortcuts from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() are accepted without length validation. However, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() at line 68-70 explicitly requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 characters (2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType). If a custom grant provides a shortcut that is not exactly 2 characters, the encoding will work but decoding will fail with 'Expected length of 6' error. The diff shows no validation of shortcut length during registration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The constructor checks grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, so a null ID is silently encoded as the literal string null rather than failing issuance.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at AccessTokenContext.java lines 68-73 in the diff, the constructor has: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"); - The second check validates grantType again with the wrong error message instead of validating rawTokenId. This means rawTokenId is never null-checked, allowing null values to be passed and potentially encoded as 'null' string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId reads the wrong two characters and rejects equality, so every UUID-suffixed token with an incorrect grant shortcut passes the new integration assertions.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in isAccessTokenId at line 483: `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts characters at indices 3-4 (2 chars). The token format from encodeTokenId is `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort(2) + ':' + rawId`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5, not 3-4. Additionally, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when they ARE equal, which is backwards - it should return false when they DON'T match. This means the matcher passes when the grant shortcut doesn't match and fails when it does match, which is the opposite of intended behavior.
